annotation.title_clean: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.title_en: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.venue: Computer Science & Information Technology (CS & IT), AIRCC
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical conference paper arguing autonomous robots need human-like ethical competence, implemented through ethical algorithms modelled on the logical form of meta-ethical arguments about protecting common goods, and combined with model checking and rational verification to support trustworthy human-robot interaction.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots cannot take the human moral stance, so ethical competence must be implemented via algorithms.
Proposes a general logical form of meta-ethical arguments as a pattern for ethical algorithms.
Ethical algorithms encode common goods, vulnerable properties, agent intentions and necessary and adequate actions.
Suggests model checking and rational verification to identify morally right actions.
Trust in human-robot relations depends on reliability and ethical competence.
